faq.q: How do I choose among the four split modes, and what does 'separators per segment' do?
faq.a: Symbol mode cuts at the delimiters you type, every N of them: set 'separators per segment' to 1 for one sentence per segment, or 3 to merge three sentences — handy for fixed-size chunks. Length mode cuts by character count; add a delimiter and the cut backs up to the nearest one so sentences stay whole (newlines become spaces first). Chinese and English modes detect sentence boundaries by language rules, one sentence per line — ideal for sentence-by-sentence translation or subtitle drafts.

faq.q: What are the character limits when splitting text for ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and translation tools?
faq.a: AI model context limits (tokens): 200K-1M. Chinese is ~1-2 chars/token (Claude more generous), English ~4 chars/token. Translation limits: Google Translate and DeepL free both 5000 chars/request. Set 'Split char count' with buffer below the target AI's token capacity.

faq.q: How do I split long posts for Twitter/X, Threads, Mastodon, or Bluesky?
faq.a: Platform limits: Twitter/X 280 chars, Threads 500, Mastodon 500, Bluesky 300, LinkedIn 3000, Tumblr 4096, Reddit posts 40000, Substack notes 500. Use 'English paragraph' mode for Latin scripts — preserves sentence integrity at word boundaries. Use Export Segment Files for sequential posting (1/N, 2/N); more than 3 segments arrive as a ZIP.

faq.q: Can I merge the segments back into one text? What is the difference between the three result buttons?
faq.a: Yes. 'Copy Merged Text' joins every segment into one text on your clipboard; 'Export Merged Text' saves that same text as a single .txt; 'Export Segment Files' writes one file per segment, packing a ZIP beyond 3. The glue is the 'Merge Separator' setting — two newlines by default, with \n, \t and \s escapes; leaving it empty falls back to that default. Note that Length and the sentence modes flatten newlines into spaces and drop blank lines, so the merged text is a fresh join, not the original layout.

faq.q: Once the chunks are split, what tools pair well for translating or further cleaning them?
faq.a: If the chunks are i18n JSON fragments (a language file split by key), use [JSON Translator](../json-translate) to batch-translate while preserving keys. For Markdown long-form (blog posts split by chapter), use [Markdown Translator](../md-translator) — it preserves code blocks and Front Matter. For heavier cleanup (dedup, regex extraction, URL pulling) before feeding chunks to AI, run them through the [Text Toolbox](../text-toolbox) first.

faq.q: How do I handle mixed Chinese/English text or non-UTF-8 files (French ISO-8859-1, Japanese Shift-JIS)?
faq.a: For mixed CJK/English, use Chinese paragraph mode — it recognizes both Chinese (。！？) and English (. ! ?) sentence endings without splitting mid-word. The Separators field takes several symbols separated by spaces and supports \n and \t escapes; it defines the cut points in Symbol mode and only aligns them in Length mode. For non-UTF-8 files (French ISO-8859-1, Japanese Shift-JIS, Korean EUC-KR), **upload the file directly** rather than pasting — encoding is auto-detected to prevent garbled output.

faq.q: Is my text uploaded to a server? Is the tool open source?
faq.a: 100% client-side: text reading, splitting, and export all happen in your browser — nothing is uploaded to any server, so sensitive content is safe. Source code is open on GitHub (rockbenben/text-splitter) for self-hosting or auditing.
